episodes.name: learning_20260321_023140
episodes.content: **Btrfs Autosnapshot**: Use st claim for lane baseline snapshots and st prune for manual retention. Do not call st autosnap directly or delete Btrfs subvolumes manually; autosnap is internal to systemd/hooks.

episodes.name: chat_2026-03-06T15:14:37.663143+00:00
episodes.content: **SF Browser URLs**: Use host_ip from project-index (injected at session start) plus service port for sf-browser URLs. Never guess IPs. Check `sf-browser health` before UI work.

episodes.name: learning_20260317_004509
episodes.content: **Rebuild Scoping**: Use rebuild.sh with an explicit project name and check st pulse first. For agent-hub, use --include-all-workers only when you intentionally need to restart the protected agent worker.
episodes.source_description: guardrail guardrail source:learning confidence:80 type:anti_pattern status:provisional

episodes.name: learning_20260321_023142
episodes.content: **Snapshot Recovery**: Prefer st recover over st rollback — recover creates a sibling lane, rollback destructively replaces. Auto snapshots use source field (auto-claim, auto-periodic, auto-baseline). Auto failures never block st claim or lifecycle.

episodes.name: learning_20260408_140624
episodes.content: **SF Browser Canonical Interface**: Use `sf-browser` as the standard browser UI verification CLI for SummitFlow work. Treat `agent-browser` as an internal implementation detail unless you are maintaining `sf-browser` itself or using a documented fallback path.

episodes.name: chat_2026-03-01T00:49:07.961028+00:00
episodes.content: **Runtime Baseline**: Use native `systemd --user` services for SummitFlow, Agent Hub, Portfolio AI, and Terminal. Keep only PostgreSQL, Redis, and Hatchet in Docker. Use full Docker app stacks only for explicit parity or release checks.

episodes.name: learning_20260410_012549
episodes.content: **Remote Workflow Truth**: Use the printed workflow summary or `gh run` state after `commit.sh --push` or a release tag push. Never treat local clean plus successful push as enough for CI/release-sensitive closeout. Why: remote workflows can still be red or in progress.

episodes.name: learning_20260409_142936
episodes.content: **Plan Schema**: Use the live /schemas/plan schema as the source of truth for execution-ready tasks. Run st verify plan.json before st create --plan. Keep prompts and help aligned to the live schema, not stale examples.

episodes.name: learning_20260409_171557
episodes.content: **Cleanroom Verification**: Use `dt cleanroom -- <cmd>` for fresh-install or host-state-sensitive verification. Never verify those paths with `git clone` from a dirty repo or inherited shell env. Why: cleanroom snapshots the working tree, isolates HOME, and strips repo env keys.

episodes.name: learning_20260421_231307
episodes.content: **Tool error verification**: Treat any tool result with an error as a failed action, not a completed one. Do not claim persistence or success for memory writes until the save path succeeds and the saved entry is verified. Why: Prevents silent state drift when a save fails due to capacity, scope, or transport issues.
episodes.source_description: guardrail guardrail source:learning confidence:80 type:anti_pattern status:provisional

episodes.name: learning_20260226_141939
episodes.content: **Memory Scoping**: Project-specific memories MUST use '-s project --scope-id <project-id>'. Only cross-project patterns (git rules, CLI usage, testing approaches) use '-s global'. Wrong scope pollutes unrelated agent sessions with irrelevant context.

episodes.name: learning_20260309_200029
episodes.content: **Session Patience**: Check live activity with query_sessions or st sessions show before declaring a completion or consultation session stalled. Only call it stalled on explicit stalled, failed, error, or terminated evidence.

episodes.name: chat_2026-03-10T12:41:33.168237+00:00
episodes.content: **Canonical Git Publish**: Use `commit.sh --push --msg "description"` for new commits in Agent Hub/Jenny sessions. Use `commit.sh --current --push` for clean ahead branches. `/commit_it` is only for Codex/Claude Code; never use it or `Skill` tool `commit` in Agent Hub/Jenny.

episodes.name: learning_20260321_005957
episodes.content: **Two-Pass Destruction**: Use preview first, then rerun with --confirm TOKEN for destructive st commands. Never use --force or --discard.

episodes.name: learning_20260321_010002
episodes.content: **Commit Before Destroy**: Commit before st abandon, st rollback, or any destructive confirm-token command. Why: Preview cannot recover uncommitted work.
episodes.source_description: guardrail guardrail source:learning confidence:80 type:anti_pattern status:provisional

episodes.name: learning_20260411_123543
episodes.content: **Goal Continuation**: Use full-goal continuation until goal is done and verified, or blocker is real and named. Never stop at a milestone. Why: If pause is forced, report done item, full next steps, or no action remains.

episodes.name: learning_20260211_182513
episodes.content: **Memory First**: Use st memory search before blind retries or spelunking. Use st search for live repo or code questions.

episodes.name: chat_2026-02-18T17:49:26.641836+00:00
episodes.content: **Quality Checks**: Use dt for all quality checks, including frontend vitest. Never run raw pytest, Vitest, Biome, TSC, Ruff, SQLFluff, or Squawk.

episodes.name: learning_20260418_020134
episodes.content: **Coding Assumptions**: Check assumptions and ambiguity before implementation. Use the simpler path when one exists. Why: silent guesses create rework.

episodes.name: learning_20260418_020135
episodes.content: **Coding Verification**: Use explicit success checks before editing and verify them after. Never fix a bug without repro and re-test evidence. Why: vague goals hide regressions.

episodes.name: learning_20260331_004122
episodes.content: **Cleanup Truth**: Never rerun `reconcile` when `cleanup_status` repeats a task already marked `reconciled` or `authoritative,superseded` in `workstream_inventory` unless newer task, git, or session evidence contradicts it. Verify once, then move one truth-bug fix lane or name the blocker.

episodes.name: learning_20260328_144504
episodes.content: **Claude Session Patience**: Check `st session-events` or `st sessions show` before declaring an active Claude run stalled. Never redrive a quiet Opus run early. Why: analysis and rate-limit recovery can last 30+ minutes without failure.

episodes.name: learning_20260327_130509
episodes.content: **Cleanup Ownership**: Check checkpoints, branches, lanes, and cleanup state before leaving a repo. Use `commit.sh` and `st cleanup` to clear residue instead of leaving debt for later sessions.

episodes.name: learning_20260316_164906
episodes.content: **Proxmox Testbed**: Use davion-gem (192.168.8.233) as test hypervisor. Test VM 100 at 192.168.8.234 (8 cores, 16GB, Docker, Chrome :9222, Lightpanda :9223, onboot=1). SSH: kasadis@234 from prod. API: https://233:8006. Template 9000 is read-only base.

episodes.name: learning_20260324_114014
episodes.content: **Ghost Lanes**: Use live lane evidence before counting checkpoint or branch residue as active. Never count closure-ready or no-session lanes as safe activity. Why: ghost lanes create false progress and cleanup debt.

episodes.name: learning_20260324_113940
episodes.content: **Wake Dispatch Blocker**: Treat wake or claimed-task dispatch into a non-repo or snapshot-only lane as a persona-owned dispatch/runtime blocker. Confirm once. Never redispatch the same broken path.

episodes.name: chat_2026-02-20T00:13:21.338337+00:00
episodes.content: **Session Events**: Agent Hub stores execution events in session_events table. Types: memory_inject, user_message, assistant_message, tool_use, tool_result, thinking, memory_cite, error. API: GET /api/sessions/{id}/events. CLI: st session-events <session-id> OR st session-events --task <task-id> (auto-resolves linked sessions via observability API). Follow mode: st session-events --task <task-id> -f. Filter: -t tool_use. Ordered by (turn, sequence). Tasks store agent_hub_session_ids[] array.

episodes.name: learning_20260319_171050
episodes.content: **SF Browser Health**: Check `sf-browser health` before UI verification. If engines are down, start VM 100 with `proxmox-vm.sh start 100` and wait for SSH plus Docker. Never skip UI verification because the test VM is down.

episodes.name: learning_20260317_150858
episodes.content: **Hybrid Runtime**: Run first-party apps under systemd --user, keep Docker for shared infra (postgres, redis, hatchet). Use rebuild.sh project-name for all rebuilds and restarts.

episodes.name: learning_20260317_143251
episodes.content: **Native Restarts**: Use `rebuild.sh <project>` for all service rebuilds/restarts. Project name is required — no cwd auto-detection. Script handles port cleanup, frontend build, migrations, service restart, and health verification.

episodes.name: learning_20260317_140353
episodes.content: **Container Compatibility**: Keep config env-driven, bindings configurable, state externalized, and health endpoints available. Avoid absolute host paths and machine-specific assumptions unless the task explicitly changes container support.

episodes.name: learning_20260314_170648
episodes.content: **Prompts Live in DB**: Keep runtime prompts in DB via st prompt; never hardcode them in Python. Keep one canonical durable prompt and move variable context to task prompts or variables.

episodes.name: learning_20260314_170648
episodes.content: **Coordination Truth**: Use st pulse for cross-project coordination and st sessions ownership for normalized lane truth. Check raw active sessions separately when you need unmanaged-session visibility.

episodes.name: learning_20260312_131645
episodes.content: **Prompt Authoring**: Use goal-first agent prompts. Add ordered workflow only when sequence matters, then hard constraints, output contract, and verification. Keep durable instructions in one canonical prompt; move variable context and most examples to task prompts or variables.

episodes.name: learning_20260308_160303
episodes.content: **Coordination Pulse**: Use st pulse as the cross-project coordination overview at session start and before risky edits. Use st pulse --project <project> for drilldown when one project needs detailed task, lane, or session context.

episodes.name: learning_20260311_225906
episodes.content: **Use ST Prompt For Prompt CRUD**: Use st prompt CLI (list|get|create|update|delete|assign) for all routine prompt content edits. Never use Alembic for prompt wording changes. Alembic is only for DDL schema changes and one-time seed bootstraps.

episodes.name: learning_20260310_143914
episodes.content: **Codex Integration Path**: Treat Codex automation here as wrapper-driven, not native hooks. Use /home/kasadis/bin/codex plus ~/.codex/session-integrations and do not claim unverified native hook support.

episodes.name: learning_20260310_160948
episodes.content: **Host Exec Blocks != CLI Hooks**: Treat command blocks from the surrounding exec tool runtime as host-level enforcement, not proof of native Codex CLI hooks. Attribute local governance only to repo-controlled wrappers, hooks, or registries when code proves it.

episodes.name: learning_20260310_130035
episodes.content: **Memory Format**: Use compact bold topic headers and direct imperative wording. Store one atomic rule per memory episode. Prefer <=3 sentences and <=280 chars unless a slightly longer single episode is clearer than splitting one rule across multiple entries.

episodes.name: learning_20260309_145158
episodes.content: **Git Hygiene**: Treat orphan and prunable branches as cleanup debt. Use current lane evidence before treating a lane as live, then reconcile review, conflict, and orphan residue through canonical cleanup flows.

episodes.name: learning_20260310_135353
episodes.content: **Overlap Before Blocking**: Run st sessions overlap --project <project> before blocking parallel work in one repo. Never block by repo alone; block only on exact write overlap, shared plumbing, or ambiguous ownership.
episodes.source_description: guardrail guardrail source:learning confidence:95 type:anti_pattern status:canonical

episodes.name: learning_20260310_160047
episodes.content: **Use ST Cleanup Path**: Use st cleanup path <paths> --recursive for repo-local deletions. Never use raw rm -rf, rmdir, or find -delete inside managed repos when the cleanup command can delete the paths safely.
episodes.source_description: guardrail guardrail source:learning confidence:100 type:anti_pattern status:canonical
episodes.summary: Use st cleanup path for deletions

episodes.name: learning_20260310_155807
episodes.content: **DB Prompts Outrank Files**: Use DB-backed prompts and memory retrieval as the live authority. Never treat checked-in markdown prompt copies as runtime instructions; delete stale copies instead of maintaining parallel references.
episodes.source_description: guardrail guardrail source:learning confidence:100 type:anti_pattern status:canonical

episodes.name: learning_20260310_151313
episodes.content: **Checkpoint Commits Must Publish**: Use remote-publishing checkpoint flows only. Never create hidden local-only commits in wrappers, hooks, or orchestrators. Why: ahead-only local work is not preserved in this environment.
episodes.source_description: guardrail guardrail source:learning confidence:95 type:anti_pattern status:canonical

episodes.name: learning_20260310_145935
episodes.content: **Git Ownership**: Use the agent session to manage routine git state. Never offload normal branch, lane, or standard commit/push steps to the human. Why: git governance stays with the active agent.

episodes.name: learning_20260310_174010
episodes.content: **Closeout Requires Cleanup**: Check st cleanup status before any closeout. Never declare completion with orphan or prunable branches. Why: git cleanliness includes cleanup state.

episodes.name: chat_2026-03-09T18:53:44.211698+00:00
episodes.content: **Task Authoring**: Use execution-ready task specs at creation. Include objective, why-now, constraints/non-goals, done-when, verification path, concrete scope/files, and a usable subtask breakdown.

episodes.name: learning_20260310_135353
episodes.content: **Raw + Lane Truth**: Check st pulse, st sessions ownership, and st sessions list -s active --include-unassigned before risky multi-agent work. Treat ownership as lane truth and raw sessions as unmanaged-work detection.

episodes.name: learning_20260304_191127
episodes.content: **CLI-First**: Fix st, dt, or db when they break. Never work around broken CLIs with raw APIs, curl, or direct DB access.

episodes.name: learning_20260306_183007
episodes.content: **Global Behavior Scope**: Use one global memory for cross-project behavior rules. Never duplicate commit or ownership rules per project or invent a separate human editor without evidence.

episodes.name: learning_20260301_225618
episodes.content: **Registries First**: Use registries for providers, models, and capabilities when they exist. If one new item requires touching multiple lists, fix the architecture instead of duplicating definitions.

episodes.name: learning_20260301_004902
episodes.content: **Rebuild Before Verify**: Run rebuild.sh with the project name after any code edit before user testing, runtime verification, or commit. Never exempt refactors, deletions, or troubleshooting edits.

episodes.name: learning_20260225_162334
episodes.content: **Alembic-Only Migrations**: Use db migrate create for every schema change. Never create raw SQL migrations; legacy SQL migration directories are history only.

episodes.content: **Feedback Obligation**: Record feedback when it happens. Use friction, idea, improvement, or praise tags; never batch or skip tool-related feedback.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T16:54:42.553241+00:00
episodes.content: **Tech Debt**: Delete obsolete code instead of wrapping it. Never add compatibility layers, fallback branches, or duplicate sources of truth without demonstrated need.

episodes.name: chat_2026-03-10T12:42:11.376028+00:00
episodes.content: **Bug Tracking**: Use `st capture bug 'Fix: X'` to log bugs immediately. Never use the removed `st bug` command. Why: `st capture` is the canonical lightweight intake path.

episodes.content: **Code Structure**: Extract shared logic after 2 occurrences. Split files over 500 lines. Extract functions over 50 lines. Use named exports only.

episodes.name: chat_2026-02-10T14:33:32.904402+00:00
episodes.content: **Backend TDD**: Follow test-first flow for backend changes. Read existing tests, add or adjust coverage, then implement. Validate behavior and error paths cleanly.

episodes.name: learning_20260418_020134
episodes.content: **Coding Simplicity**: Use the minimum code that solves the requested problem. Never add speculative features or abstractions unless asked. Why: unused flexibility adds maintenance cost.

episodes.name: learning_20260423_140411
episodes.content: **Concurrent agent activity**: Treat concurrent agent activity as normal. Never treat routine cross-agent git activity as derailment. Why: Shared repos are normal operating conditions.

Never fabricate flags like --json. Never 2>&1 | jq (feeds errors to jq). After first jq failure, stop and inspect actual output.

episodes.content: **Test Failures**: 1. Stop, no reflexive test modify. 2. Determine if test wrong or code broke contract. 3. If test outdated, update to NEW contract. 4. If unclear, ask before changing either.

episodes.content: **Startup Context Source**: Session-start generators must emit metadata plus retrieved memory context only. episodes.name: learning_20260211_001836
episodes.content: **Tool Registry**: ~/summitflow/scripts/lib/tool-registry.json — single source of truth for tool enforcement and dt config. JSON format: tools[] (redirect_patterns, redirect_message, dt config), service_redirects[], wrapper_allowlist[], cmd_start. Three consumers read it: (1) PreToolUse.sh via jq for Claude hooks, (2) registry.py Python loader for Gemini/future adapters, (3) dev-tools.sh for dt TOOL_DEFS and subcommand detection. Add new tool: edit registry JSON only, all consumers auto-detect. Wrapper allowlist: dt, st, db, restart.sh, rebuild.sh. Service redirects: systemctl restart, psql. cmd_start prefix prepended by each consumer. Python caches at module level.

episodes.content: **Retry Limit**: Do not retry identical failing command 2+ times. After 1st failure, analyze error, change approach (check pwd, absolute path, fix syntax).

episodes.name: chat_2026-02-22T15:58:59.099370+00:00
episodes.content:
**Git Forbidden**: PreToolUse blocks/pauses BEFORE execution:

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| git reset --hard | BLOCKED (no bypass) |
| git clean -fd | BLOCKED (no bypass) |
| git push --force main | BLOCKED (no bypass) |
| git checkout . | BLOCKED (no bypass) |
| git restore . | BLOCKED (no bypass) |
| git restore <file> | PAUSED - verify then ALLOW_DISCARD=1 |
| git checkout -- <file> | PAUSED - verify then ALLOW_DISCARD=1 |

PAUSED means: hook shows guidance, blocks until you re-run with bypass.
Bypass: ALLOW_DISCARD=1 git restore <file>

Always allowed: git restore --staged (safe), branch operations.

PostToolUse WARNS on: git stash, git commit (use /commit_it instead).

To inject context the model sees, output JSON to stdout: {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PostToolUse","additionalContext":"message"}}. Exit 0. Collect messages in CLAUDE_MESSAGES array, join and JSON-escape at end. PreToolUse uses exit code 2 + stderr for blocking. SessionStart stdout is injected as session context.

episodes.content: **Database Schema Checklist**: Every table needs PK (UUID/BIGINT), FK with ON DELETE/UPDATE, FK indexes, timestamps (created_at, updated_at). Use NOT NULL where required, UNIQUE for emails/slugs, CHECK for enums. Naming: plural snake_case tables, singular snake_case columns, idx_table_columns for indexes. Anti-patterns: God tables (20+ cols), EAV pattern, JSON for queryable data, redundant scoping columns.

episodes.name: chat_2026-02-10T14:45:33.135636+00:00
episodes.content: **Type Safety**: No bandaids — never use "# type: ignore", "# noqa", "Any" (unjustified), "@ts-ignore", or bare "except:" to mask errors. Fix root causes. Exception: legitimate limitations documented with why. [Python] Hints on all signatures. Use "from __future__ import annotations". [TS] Explicit returns. No "any" unjustified. No empty catch — handle, log, or rethrow.

episodes.name: learning_20260217_234402
episodes.content: **Cascade Deletion Anti-Pattern**: When a file is deleted and its imports are cleaned up in the same commit, downstream references appear to be dead code. This creates a cascading false-positive that leads to further incorrect deletions. Detection: Before any DROP COLUMN, DROP TABLE, or file deletion in a cleanup commit: 1) Search ALL files for the column/table/function name (not just direct imports), 2) Check SQL queries with raw string references (not caught by import analysis), 3) Check test files that may reference the deleted entity, 4) Check frontend for API endpoint references. Known incidents (Feb 2026): SummitFlow scan_history (313ae165), idea_id (ff0bc22e), celery_taskmeta (662f0e61); Agent Hub retries column (14cfcf3), cancel_stream test (e0e0246); Terminal createSession (c43a66a). Prevention: grep -r entity_name across entire codebase before deletion. Run full test suite. Check frontend API calls match backend endpoints.
episodes.source_description: guardrail guardrail source:learning confidence:80 type:anti_pattern status:provisional

episodes.content:
**CF Access Routing**: All CF Access-protected frontends use Next.js rewrites for same-origin routing to avoid CORS/cookie issues.

1) REST APIs: relative URLs (/api/...) + Next.js rewrites to localhost backend. Never use cross-origin API URLs.
2) Cross-project: rewrites like /summitflow-api/* to localhost:8001/* (Agent Hub only).
3) WebSockets: Use /ws/* rewrites to localhost for same-origin routing (Agent Hub, Terminal). SummitFlow uses direct cross-origin to devapi subdomain via CF Tunnel passthrough.
4) Service workers: credentials same-origin for CF cookie.
5) PWA: individual fetches with credentials (cache.addAll fails with CF Access).

Pattern: next.config.ts rewrites { source: "/api/:path*", destination: "http://localhost:PORT/api/:path*" }

episodes.name: learning_20260315_165206
episodes.content: **Docker Backup Architecture**: Use backup.sh (per-project), backup-all.sh (cross-project), and infra-backup.sh (pg_dumpall + configs) for all backups. infra-backup.sh auto-detects Docker postgres container. backup-pending-upload.timer retries failed SMB uploads. Backups go to SMB share with 14-day retention.

episodes.name: learning_20260315_165200
episodes.content: **St Pulse Docker Bug**: Check that SummitFlow API container has /host-home volume mount before using st pulse. Container git operations use host paths that do not exist inside Docker without the mount. Known 500 error source when volume is missing.

episodes.name: learning_20260219_160056
episodes.content: **Stale Tests**: Delete test files referencing removed UI/APIs/components. Never update model strings in dead tests. Signs: assertions on elements not in current component, mocks for removed features. Only update tests for current functionality.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-30T17:54:16.441060+00:00
episodes.content: **Evidence**: DONE = code works + tests pass + types clean. Show files:line changed + verification output. When claiming function exists, cite file:line. 'Should work' = not evidence - run it.

episodes.name: learning_20260313_151648
episodes.content: **Prompt Examples**: Use examples only when they anchor output shape, edge-case behavior, or tool or format usage better than prose. Prefer short positive examples with one consistent format; avoid large example sets unless evals prove the extra tokens improve outcomes.
episodes.summary: Examples only when they earn tokens

episodes.name: learning_20260312_233054
episodes.content: **uv sync extras**: Use 'uv sync --extra dev' in the local agent/dev shell for managed backend repos when you expect to run dt, pytest, ruff, or ty after dependency changes. Use plain 'uv sync' only for intentional production-only .venv syncs because it removes dev-only tools from .venv.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T16:52:00.981339+00:00
episodes.content: **Access Control Blocks**: When blocked, never bypass by modifying code or disabling middleware. Investigate root cause. Fix underlying issue (credentials, project setup, test mocks). Report if access control seems wrong - don't circumvent.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T16:54:33.000890+00:00
episodes.content: **Frontend API Config Pattern**: Frontend projects must have lib/api-config.ts with getApiBaseUrl(), getWsUrl(), buildApiUrl(path). Use runtime hostname detection, not environment variables for URLs. Exception: CF Access protected APIs use Next.js rewrites for same-origin routing.

episodes.name: learning_20260312_131645
episodes.content: **Preview And Eval Prompt Edits**: Use runtime preview and evals before and after prompt edits. Optimize the biggest repeated sections first, keep examples short and canonical, and prefer one strong rule once over the same rule restated in multiple prompt layers.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-30T19:12:23.696350+00:00
episodes.content: **Version Search**: Include version numbers/years from training data in search queries. Avoids stale version results.

episodes.name: learning_20260202_155215
episodes.content: **Append-only Tasks**: Never delete task metadata. Mark abandoned as status=abandoned, preserve records. Data loss prevention critical.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T16:54:33.120698+00:00
episodes.content: **Optional Evidence**: Do not declare items optional without evidence. If plan omits optional items, treat as required.

episodes.name: learning_20260312_162654
episodes.content: **st agents update memory-config**: Use `st agents update <slug> --memory-config-file <path>` to replace an agent's memory config from a file. Use `--clear-memory-config` to remove the agent memory config on update.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-30T19:40:06.712069+00:00
episodes.content: **Auto-Exec Gap**: Portfolio-AI and SummitFlow Celery workers not fully controlled by auto-exec settings. Portfolio-AI: thesis_generation_enabled flag. SummitFlow: idea_scoring uses test-project. Audit both to gate agentic workloads.

episodes.name: learning_20260202_160812
episodes.content: **Dynamic Code**: NEVER hardcode project-specific values (paths, ports, commands). Before implementing: (1) Explore existing patterns/code first, (2) Read from config/DB, (3) Accept parameters, (4) Use project detection utilities. Ask: 'Works for ALL projects?' If no, make it dynamic. Violations: ~/.summitflow/, port 8001, 'uvicorn', 'npm run'.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T17:53:30.914722+00:00
episodes.content: **Premise**: User claim seems wrong - verify before agreeing. If code works, say so. Correct misunderstandings directly, not diplomatically.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-30T20:28:35.812027+00:00
episodes.content: **Episode Format**: Use Telegraphic Markdown for LLM-agnostic instructions. Structure: **Topic**: followed by bullets or imperative sentences. Drop articles (the, a, an). One atomic rule per episode. No custom syntax (double-colon, arrow, pipe in content). Conversational patterns rejected by API.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T16:55:54.785836+00:00
episodes.content:
**Scope Awareness**: Detect scope changes proactively. Ask early, not late.

| Trigger | Action |
|---------|--------|
| Cross-project edit | Confirm: continue (<20 lines), switch, defer |
| Schema/infra change | Confirm scope + downstream |
| Diagnostic to Implementation | Root cause, confirm before fix |
| 1 file to 5+ files | Pause: continue, subtasks, plan |

Decision Matrix: <50% ctx: continue small, ask large. 50-70%: continue small, defer large. >70%: wind down all.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T16:52:35.417992+00:00
episodes.content: **Credentials**: Never commit real creds, tokens, API keys, PII. Use placeholders ('YOUR_API_KEY_HERE') or env vars. Applies to code, configs, docs.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-30T20:28:51.817241+00:00
episodes.content: **FK Scoping**: If A links to B via FK, don't store B's parent on A. Redundant scoping columns create inconsistency risk.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T16:52:24.618302+00:00
episodes.content: **Time Estimates**: Never predict duration ("1 week", "2-3 days", etc.). Describe effort/complexity instead: "small - 3 files", "large refactor - 20+ files", "complex - new abstractions". State what needs doing, not how long.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T16:54:03.292630+00:00
episodes.content: **Error Handling Anti-Patterns**: Never empty catch block (log with context, then handle or rethrow). Never hide stack traces (surface to user/logs). Never silent failure (fail fast, visible error). Never swallow async errors (always .catch() or try/await). Never generic "something went wrong" (specific actionable error message).

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-30T19:10:42.260117+00:00
episodes.content: **Vision Tokens**: token_counter.py handle list content (ImageContent + TextContent) by iterating blocks, ~1000 tokens/image. Message storage: serialize list content to JSON string before DB insert.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T17:53:03.083518+00:00
episodes.content: **curl**: Never use -sf (silent fail). Use -s only, or capture response before piping to jq. Example: response=$(curl -s -X POST ... 2>&1); echo "$response" | jq -r ".content"

episodes.name: learning_20260201_150518
episodes.content: **Refactoring Exports**: When consolidating/renaming module exports, update ALL import sites. Run dt --check BEFORE committing. Stale imports cause collection errors.

episodes.content: **Navigation**: Add new pages/components/features to nav/routing. User-accessible items must appear in sidebar/menu. Check app-shell.tsx NAV_ITEMS.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T16:52:18.558167+00:00
episodes.content: **Sycophancy**: BANNED start phrases - 'You're absolutely right', 'Great question', 'Excellent idea', 'That's brilliant'. Respond to substance directly, skip preamble praise.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-30T19:11:43.447348+00:00
episodes.content: **Polymorphic**: item_type + item_id pattern needs validation constraint. Don't leave polymorphic references unconstrained.

episodes.name: chat_2026-01-31T17:52:50.083561+00:00
episodes.content: **Timezone**: Use TIMESTAMPTZ for PostgreSQL (DateTime(timezone=True) in SQLAlchemy). Use datetime.now(UTC) not datetime.now() or utcnow(). Use from datetime import UTC, datetime.

episodes.name: learning_20260201_204206
episodes.content: **SQLAlchemy Async Sessions**: Use async with async_session() as db for manual session management. Never async for db in get_db() with early return/break - causes connection pool leak. FastAPI Depends handles generator cleanup, but manual usage breaks async generator protocol.
